name: Campbell's Covered Bridge
facts: Campbell's Covered Bridge, built in 1909 by Charles Irwin Willis, honors grist mill owner Alexander Lafayette Campbell, whose mill still stands nearby and whose legacy lives on in the bridge's name.
The 38‑foot long, 12‑foot wide structure showcases a rare four‑span Howe truss, combining vertical iron rods with diagonal pine timbers for a distinctive, sturdy design.
After motorized traffic was banned in the early 1980s, the bridge received two restorations—first by the Crescent Garden Club in 1964 and again in 1990—preserving its historic charm.
